note: Declared scope for the S0.8 exit test. Every declaration here is self-verifying: tools/test_s0_8_exit.py asserts each one STILL APPLIES, so a stale entry is an error rather than a harmless leftover (Doc 7 section 3).
what_s08_claims: The dependency graph the package actually imports is resolvable, pinned by version and sha256 in requirements/hybrid_stack.lock, and demonstrated to install and import in a clean environment. It does NOT claim to have closed B-4, which is about the davinci HPC environment specifically.
no_transform_id: S0.8 introduces NO transform. It adds new infrastructure under byte-identity rule clause (3) and changes the content of no pre-existing file except declared tooling. There is nothing to invert and nothing to log, so no T-number is allocated. S0.5 was the same shape.

finding_H8.statement: The 'historically conflicting pins' the roadmap blocks on DO NOT CONFLICT at current versions.
finding_H8.evidence: pip resolves LFPy 2.3.7, hybridLFPy 0.2, neuron 9.0.1 and nest-simulator 3.10.0 into ONE environment; `pip check` reports 'No broken requirements found'; and all eleven third-party modules the package imports load in a single process, in the order driver.py requires. Measured 21 July 2026.
finding_H8.consequence: TEEG_03 section 3.2 specifies TWO lockfiles. One is delivered instead. Two would be machinery for a conflict that does not exist, and worse, two environments could not run driver.py at all -- see finding_H10.
finding_H8.status: PROPOSED, needs ratification: one lockfile supersedes the roadmap's two.
finding_H8.caveat: Measured with PyPI wheels on Ubuntu/glibc2.39. The historical conflict was plausibly a CONDA and build-toolchain conflict on the cluster, which this measurement cannot speak to. H-8 refutes the pip-metadata form of the claim, not the cluster form.

finding_H9.statement: hybridLFPy 0.2 cannot be installed by a modern pip without two workarounds, and neither is documented upstream.
finding_H9.detail: It is sdist-only. Its build backend is poetry.core.masonry.api, but its build path imports numpy while declaring no build requirements. Under PEP-517 isolated builds the install fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'; with --no-build-isolation it fails with BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'poetry.core.masonry.api'.
finding_H9.recipe: Install poetry-core, numpy and Cython FIRST, then install with --no-build-isolation. Recorded in the validation record under extra_steps_required and in the lockfile header.
finding_H9.why_it_matters: This is a latent blocker that would have surfaced on the cluster, during S1, as an opaque build failure. It is a property of the package, not of any environment, so it applies to davinci too.

finding_H10.statement: The two simulator stacks are not merely both required; they must be CO-RESIDENT IN ONE PROCESS, in a specified import order.
finding_H10.evidence: towards_eeg/hybrid/driver.py imports neuron at L39, nest at L41, hybridLFPy at L43. Its own comments say why: L39 'NEURON compiled with MPI must be imported before NEST and mpi4py', L41 'Import not used, but done in order to ensure correct execution'.
finding_H10.consequence: A two-environment split is not merely unnecessary, it is unusable: neither half could run driver.py. This is the strongest argument for the single lockfile, and it is a property of the CODE rather than of any package index, so it holds on the cluster too.
finding_H10.what_no_lockfile_can_express: The import ORDER. A lockfile pins what is installed, not the sequence in which a module imports it. The validation record therefore tests the order explicitly.

b4_what_remains.status: B-4 REMAINS OPEN. S0.8 does not close it.
b4_what_remains.why: The roadmap's exit criterion is met in a clean Linux venv from PyPI wheels. That is not the davinci conda environment, and two entries in the lockfile are actively WRONG for an HPC node.

entries_wrong_for_hpc.openmpi==5.0.10: A PyPI-wheel MPI runtime. On a cluster MPI comes from a module and must match the interconnect; a pip-installed MPI will not use the high-speed fabric and may not cooperate with the scheduler's mpirun.
entries_wrong_for_hpc.neuron==9.0.1: The PyPI wheel is NOT built with MPI. driver.py L39 requires NEURON compiled with MPI, so on davinci NEURON is expected to be a module, not this wheel.

the_three_questions_the_roadmap_blocks_o.is NEURON a module or a pip install: ANSWERED IN PART: it is pip-installable, and the wheel imports. But the wheel is not MPI-enabled, so for THIS code it is very likely a module. Confirm on davinci.
the_three_questions_the_roadmap_blocks_o.is NEST reachable: ANSWERED: yes. nest-simulator 3.10.0 publishes manylinux wheels for cp39-cp313 and installs and imports cleanly. NEST no longer requires a source build.
the_three_questions_the_roadmap_blocks_o.the real pip freeze: STILL OPEN. Only you can run it.

commands_to_run_on_davinci: conda activate <the env>; python -c 'import neuron, nest, LFPy, hybridLFPy, mpi4py; print(neuron.__version__, nest.__version__, LFPy.__version__, mpi4py.__version__)'
conda activate <the env>; pip freeze | sort
python -c "from mpi4py import MPI; print(MPI.Get_library_version())"   # which MPI is actually linked
python -c "import neuron; print(neuron.h.nrnmpi_init)"                  # is NEURON MPI-enabled
b4_what_remains.what_to_do_with_the_output: Paste it into a chat. The lockfile then gains an HPC sibling, and B-4 closes. Until then hybrid_stack.lock is the CI/reference environment and is labelled as such.

pyproject_still_declares_no_dependencies.decision: PROPOSED, needs ratification: pyproject.toml continues to declare zero runtime dependencies even though a validated set now exists.
pyproject_still_declares_no_dependencies.rationale: Declaring them would make `pip install towards_eeg` attempt to install neuron and nest-simulator from PyPI. On davinci that is the WRONG action -- NEURON is expected to come from a module built with MPI, and a pip wheel would shadow it. A package that forces the wrong simulator build on an HPC node is worse than one that declares nothing and is accompanied by a lockfile.
pyproject_still_declares_no_dependencies.alternative_considered: An optional extra, e.g. [project.optional-dependencies] reference = [...]. Deferred: it would still need a decision about what the default install does, and B-4 is the right place to settle that.

import_surface.rule: Every third-party top-level module imported anywhere under towards_eeg/ must be covered by the lockfile, or excluded by declaration below.

excluded.google: google.colab, imported by towards_eeg/connectome/connectivity_buildup.py. A Colab runtime module, not a deployable dependency; it does not exist on PyPI in the form imported. That file is unimportable by construction anyway -- defect class O10, ratified at S0.7 (N-23) and assigned to S1/S3.
excluded.nest_simulation: A hybridLFPy EXAMPLE module, not a distribution. Shipped inside the hybridLFPy examples tree, not importable from the installed package. Belongs to the S1/S3 work that untangles driver.py.
excluded.params_evoked_with_EEG: A sibling module of the pre-S0.4 layout, now towards_eeg/hybrid/params.py. The import is a stale intra-tree reference inside driver.py; rewriting it is a content operation, forbidden in S0. Assigned to S1/S3.

import_surface.local_module_note: The last three are NOT PyPI distributions and no lockfile could carry them. They are recorded here so that a future reader does not go looking for them on an index.
